# ActionWheels

[![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/coffeemkr0/ActionWheels?label=latest%20release&sort=semver&cacheSeconds=300)](https://github.com/coffeemkr0/ActionWheels/releases/latest)
[![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/coffeemkr0/ActionWheels/total?label=downloads&cacheSeconds=300)](https://github.com/coffeemkr0/ActionWheels/releases)
[![Tests](https://github.com/coffeemkr0/ActionWheels/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/coffeemkr0/ActionWheels/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](https://github.com/coffeemkr0/ActionWheels/blob/main/LICENSE)

**Radial, customizable action bars for WoW Classic-era clients (Interface 16001).** Press a key and a wheel of actions appears at your cursor. Click a slice to cast a spell, use an item, run a macro, command your pet or open another wheel. It works in combat.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Download** | [**Latest release**](https://github.com/coffeemkr0/ActionWheels/releases/latest) · [All releases](https://github.com/coffeemkr0/ActionWheels/releases) |
| **What changed** | [Changelog](https://github.com/coffeemkr0/ActionWheels/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) |
| **Need help?** | [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) · [Report a problem](https://github.com/coffeemkr0/ActionWheels/issues) |

> **1.0.0, the first release.** Tested in the game on a Classic-era client. If something misbehaves, `/aw debug` and the [troubleshooting table](#troubleshooting) are the place to start, and an [issue](https://github.com/coffeemkr0/ActionWheels/issues) with what it prints helps a lot.

## Install
1. Download the latest **ActionWheels-x.y.z.zip** from the [latest release](https://github.com/coffeemkr0/ActionWheels/releases/latest) and unzip it. Copy the whole `ActionWheels` folder into `Interface/AddOns/` (the folder name must be exactly `ActionWheels`, with `ActionWheels.toc` directly inside it).
2. Start the game (new files and icons only load on a full restart, so don't rely on `/reload` for a first install). Press **Esc > Key Bindings > AddOns > ActionWheels** and bind **Action wheel (open / hold)**. (`/aw keys` opens the key bindings.)
3. Type `/aw` (or click the minimap button) to open the editor.

## Using the wheel
- **Open:** press your key. Toggle mode: press again to close. Hold mode: the wheel shows while the key is held. **Auto** mode: hold in combat, press-to-open out of combat, on the same key (`Settings > Key behaviour`, or `/aw mode toggle|hold|auto`).
- **Click a slice** to run it. Item, macro and pet slices close the wheel right away. A **spell** slice stays open until the spell actually casts (so you can keep clicking if the first try is blocked), then closes; in combat the game won't let an addon hide the wheel, so close it with your key or by clicking outside. Change this under Settings > *After clicking a spell* or `/aw close success|click|never`. The slice darkens while pressed, flashes white on click and green when the cast is confirmed.
- Click outside the wheel to close it.
- **Mouse wheel:** scroll while the wheel is open to switch wheels (up = previous). It stops at the first and last wheel. Turn it off or reverse it in Settings or with `/aw scroll on|off|reverse`.
- **Which wheel the key opens:** the last one you used (the default, remembered across sessions), or the wheel you are editing (`Settings > The key opens`, `/aw opens selected|last`). A wheel with an auto condition such as `[mounted]` still wins while its condition holds.
- **More than one wheel:** use the `<` `>` arrows in the centre, or bind **Next wheel / Previous wheel**. A slot can open another wheel; that wheel has a **back** button.
- Each slice shows its **cooldown**, **charges / item count**, and is **grey** when unusable, **blue** without mana and **red** when your target is out of range.

## Opening the wheel with the mouse
No keyboard needed. All of these work in combat:
- **A "last wheel" button on screen:** `/aw launcher` (or Settings) shows a small movable button that opens the wheel you used last.
- **A button for each wheel:** in the editor's Wheels tab tick *Movable on-screen button for this wheel* (or `/aw launcher wheel` for the wheel you're editing). Each wheel's button remembers its own position.
- **On an action bar:** a frame can't be dragged onto a bar, so ActionWheels makes a tiny macro for you. In the editor press **Put on action bar** (Settings has **Last wheel -> bar**, or type `/aw macro [last|first|<wheel>]`). The macro lands on your cursor: click an action bar slot to drop it. By hand, the macro line is `/click ActionWheelsOpenLast`, `/click ActionWheelsOpen` (first wheel) or `/click ActionWheelsOpen2` (the 2nd wheel, up to 8).
- **Moving and locking:** Shift + drag moves any of the buttons (out of combat). Lock them in Settings or with `/aw launcher lock`. `/aw launcher reset` returns them to their start positions.
- **Where it opens:** a wheel opened from an **action bar** macro appears at the **screen centre** (the bar is at the screen edge); change it in Settings > *Action bar buttons open* or `/aw barat cursor|center`. The **on-screen buttons** follow the normal *Opens at* setting, so they open where you put them if that is set to the cursor.
- Click outside the wheel, or the button again, to close it.

## Cooldown strip: see when a spell is ready without opening the wheel
A small row of icons on screen (the **Tracker** tab, or `/aw tracker`) shows your cooldowns even with the wheel closed:
- **Always show a spell:** tick **On the cooldown strip** on its slot in the Wheels tab. It stays on screen, dimmed with a swirl and countdown while cooling down, and green-bordered when ready.
- **Long cooldowns automatically:** with *Add spells with long cooldowns automatically* on, any spell on your wheels whose cooldown is at least the number of seconds you set (30 by default) appears while it cools down and for a few seconds after it is ready.
- **Ready alert:** the icon flashes (and optionally plays a sound) when a spell comes off cooldown.
- **Moving it:** **Shift + drag** any icon of the strip. Or tick *Unlock* (or `/aw tracker unlock`) to show a blue box you can drag even when nothing is on cooldown, then lock it again. Choose the icon size and which way the row grows. It isn't clickable, and it works in combat. Items are not tracked yet.

## Editing on the wheel itself
**Right-click a slice** (out of combat) for a small menu: **Edit slot...** (opens the editor on that slot), **Swap with another slot...** (then left-click the slot to swap with; right-click cancels; it works within one wheel) and **Clear slot**.

## `#showtooltip` macros
A macro slot whose text starts with `#showtooltip Aimed Shot` (or just `#showtooltip`, meaning the first `/cast` or `/use`) shows that spell's icon, cooldown, charges, usable / range state and active-buff glow. Conditionals work and are evaluated live while the wheel is open, e.g. `#showtooltip [mod:shift] Hunter's Mark; Aimed Shot`. Remove the line to use your own icon.

## Setting up slots
Open the editor (`/aw` or the minimap button), **Wheels** tab:
- **Drag a spell** from your spellbook, an **item** from your bags or a **macro** onto a slot in the ring. This also works on the real wheel while it is open.
- An item slot is about the item, not one stack: it uses whichever stack of that item is in your bags, shows the **total** count across all stacks, and keeps working when one stack runs out.
- Or click a slot and fill in the form: type (Spell / Item / Macro / Pet / Wheel), value, optional label and icon.
- Use **New / Delete / Copy wheel**, **Move <  >** (reorders wheels), the `<` `>` picker and the `-` `+` buttons to manage wheels and their size (4 to 12 slots, up to 8 wheels). Reordering changes the paging order and the numbers in `/click ActionWheelsOpen2` macros.
- Each slot also has a **Border colour** and **Swap <  >** buttons (swap with the previous / next slot).
- **Opens first when:** a macro condition such as `[mounted]`, `[combat]` or `[stance:1]` makes that wheel open first while it holds. Otherwise the wheel you are editing opens first.

**Look** tab: button size, ring radius, wheel scale, text size, centre-controls size and sounds. **Settings** tab: open behaviour and position, button size, ring radius, wheel scale, the minimap button, separate wheels for this character, key bindings, restore the starter wheel. **Share** tab: export one or all wheels as text and import them (macros from an import are shown to you first).

### Slash commands
| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `/aw` | Open the editor |
| `/aw set 1 spell Aimed Shot` | Cast a spell |
| `/aw set 2 item Hearthstone` | Use an item |
| `/aw set 3 macro /cast Hunter's Mark` | Run macro text |
| `/aw set 4 pet attack` | Pet command: attack, follow, stay, passive, defensive, aggressive, assist |
| `/aw set 8 wheel Extra` | A slot that opens another wheel (name or number) |
| `/aw clear 3`, `/aw list`, `/aw slots 10` | Manage slots |
| `/aw wheels`, `/aw wheel new Name` / `select <n>` / `rename Name` / `delete` | Manage wheels |
| `/aw wheel auto [mounted]` (or `off`) | Open the selected wheel first when a condition holds |
| `/aw mode hold`, `/aw at center`, `/aw scale 1.2` | Open behaviour and size |
| `/aw open [first\|last\|<wheel>]` | Open a wheel from chat (out of combat only) |
| `/aw swap 1 2` | Swap two slots of the current wheel |
| `/aw wheel move up\|down`, `/aw wheel copy` | Reorder or copy the current wheel |
| `/aw sounds` | Toggle the soft tick and click sounds |
| `/aw minimap`, `/aw keys`, `/aw reset` | Minimap button, key bindings, restore the starter wheel |

## How combat works
Spells, items and macros are protected in combat, so every slice is a secure action button and the key binding is a secure click handler. Opening, closing, switching wheels and running slices all work in combat. **Editing is locked in combat**: the editor closes when combat starts and changes made by command wait until combat ends.

## Troubleshooting
| Problem | Try this |
|---|---|
| Nothing happens when I press my key | Esc > Key Bindings > AddOns > ActionWheels: check the key is set and not used by another addon (`/aw keys` opens it) |
| Clicking a slice does nothing | Run `/aw debug` and click once: the chat line shows what the slice received. Check the spell or item name matches your spellbook / bags |
| The wheel stays open in combat after a spell | By design: the game won't let an addon hide the wheel in combat, and a spell slice waits until it casts. Close it with your key or by clicking outside, or use *Hold* / *Auto* key behaviour (release the key to close), or set *After clicking a spell* to *Close right away* |
| The active-Aspect highlight is wrong in combat | The game hides buffs from addons in combat, so it follows your own casts and removal events. It corrects itself when combat ends. `/aw buffs` shows what each source reports |
| An icon is a green box or a question mark | Restart the game fully (new files and icons only load on a restart). For a spell, check the name; `/aw inspect <spell>` shows what the game reports |
| The wheel opens half off-screen | Set *Opens at: Screen centre* (Settings), or place your open button away from the screen edge |
| An action bar macro for a wheel opens the wrong one | `/click ActionWheelsOpen<n>` uses the wheel's position in the list; reordering or deleting wheels changes it. Press **Put on action bar** again |
| **Put on action bar** says the macro list is full | Delete an unused macro, or type `/click ActionWheelsOpenLast` into a macro yourself |
| A spell I expect is missing from the cooldown strip | Tick **On the cooldown strip** on its slot, or lower *Long means at least* in the Tracker tab. Spells with no reported cooldown length are only added after you have seen them cool down once |
| I can't edit in combat | By design: editing and the settings window are locked in combat |
| I want to start over | Settings > **Restore starter wheel** (or `/aw reset`) |
| Something else looks wrong | `/aw debug` prints slice and click details; open an issue with what it prints |

## Development
```bash
pip install lupa
python tests/run_tests.py
scripts/package.sh
```
**Releasing:** bump `## Version:` in `ActionWheels.toc`, add a `## <version>` section to `CHANGELOG.md`, and push to `main`. The *Auto release* workflow runs the tests, builds `ActionWheels-<version>.zip`, creates the `v<version>` tag and publishes the release with that changelog section as the notes. It only acts when the version line changes, and never touches an existing tag. To publish the current version by hand: Actions > *Auto release* > *Run workflow*. (Pushing a `v*` tag yourself still works: the *Release* workflow attaches the zip.)

releases.notes:
**The first release.** Radial, customizable action bars: press a key and a wheel of actions opens at your cursor; click a slice to cast a spell, use an item, run a macro, command your pet, or open another wheel. It works in combat.

- **Slots:** spells, items (found by ID, so any stack in your bags works and counts add up), macros (with `#showtooltip`), pet commands and sub-wheels. Drag spells, items and macros onto a slot, or fill them in with the editor or `/aw set`.
- **Wheels:** 4 to 12 slots, up to 8 wheels, paging with arrows, keys or the mouse wheel (which stops at the first and last wheel). Reorder, copy, rename; per-slot border colours; share wheels as text; optional separate wheels per character.
- **Live slices:** cooldown swirl (also in combat), charges and item counts, grey / blue / red for unusable / no mana / out of range, a gold highlight and the active icon for an active Aspect, tooltips, click feedback.
- **Opening it:** toggle, hold, or **Auto** (hold in combat, press-to-open out of combat) on one key; open at the cursor or screen centre; the key can open the last wheel you used. Open it with the mouse from an on-screen button (the last wheel, or one per wheel) or from an action bar macro.
- **Cooldown strip:** a small on-screen row of spell cooldowns, visible with the wheel closed, with a ready flash and sound. Pick spells by hand, or let long cooldowns appear automatically.
- **Editing:** a settings window (Wheels, Settings, Look, Tracker, Share), right-click a slice to edit or swap it, minimap button. Editing is locked in combat.
- Everything above also has `/aw` slash commands (`/aw` for the list) and is covered by an automatic test suite.
